title: Launch pulse & backfill schedule for multi-surface deliveries
creator: Priya Nair
description:
Summary: Define a repeatable 'launch pulse' rhythm plus a backfill lane to coordinate feature releases across runtime, console, and API surfaces. Goal is to reduce cross-team friction, avoid last-minute conflicts, and provide clear contingency lanes when one surface slips.

Scope: planning and operational runbook for launches that touch any combination of runtime (serving runtime changes, kernel/kernel-selection logic), console (dashboards, rollout controls, UI), and API (contract, new endpoints, structured output). Not including independent infra-only ops that don't change product-facing behavior.

Deliverables:
- Shared launch pulse calendar and cadence (biweekly alignments + hot lanes) with ownership per pulse
- Backfill lanes (3-day and 2-week) definition and automated gating for spillover items
- Launch gating checklist per surface (perf SLO, e2e tests, canary metrics, security/compliance signoff)
- Rollout choreography templates: canary % schedule, observability watchlist, rollback triggers, and communication templates
- Playbook for automated channel updates (Slack + release-notes) and customer-impact escalation paths

Owners & Roles:
- PM (release owner): Priya Nair — coordinate cross-surface slot assignments, run pre-launch gate
- Surface leads: Runtime: Marcus Lopez; Console: Meera Patel; API: Daniel Kim — surface-specific readiness and post-launch verification
- Launch Ops: Ethan Morales — calendar, gating automation, rollout orchestration tools
- QA/Perf: SRE/Perf team (ENG-4123) — perf signoff and load testing

Gating criteria (must be green to enter pulse):
- Runtime: p95 latency within expected window and no >1% error regression vs baseline; KV cache regression tests pass
- Console: dashboard rendering <250ms for key views; rollout controls operational in staging
- API: contract tests + structured-output validations pass; schema migration strategy documented

Canary schedule example (template):
- Day 0: 1% traffic for 2 hours (smoke checks)
- Day 0 (after smoke): 10% for 4 hours (monitoring signals)
- Day 1: 25% for 6 hours
- Day 2: 100% if no critical signals
Rollback triggers: >2x error rate vs baseline sustained for >10m, p95 latency regression >30% for 15m, or failed automated alerts from model quality evals.

Backfill lanes:
- 3-day backfill: for small regressions or staging-only blockers; slot reserved next pulse for final cut
- 2-week backfill: for cross-surface dependencies that need coordinated fixes; includes pre-booked calendar slot and dedicated QA window

Monitoring & success metrics:
- Deployment success rate per pulse (target 98%)
- Time-to-fully-deployed for items scheduled in pulse (median <72h)
- Number of cross-surface conflicts detected pre-pulse vs post-pulse (target: pre-detect >80%)
- Customer-facing incidents attributable to launch (target: 0 critical incidents per quarter)

Communication plan:
- Publish pulse calendar (Google Calendar) and pulse playbook (Confluence)
- Weekly sync 30m cross-surface triage the week prior to pulse (owners only)
- Day-of roll call + postmortem window reserved 48h after major pulses

Risks & mitigations:
- Risk: surface slips cause cascading delays —> Mitigation: backfill lanes + automated gating to prevent blocking unrelated surfaces
- Risk: unclear ownership for mixed-surface changes —> Mitigation: new metadata on tickets to mark primary surface owner and release owner
- Risk: perf regressions in runtime after canary —> Mitigation: forced rollback policy and immediate hotfix lane with SLA for bugfix deployment

Next steps / Action items:
1) Create canonical calendar and Confluence pulse playbook (owner: Ethan Morales) — due 2026-03-05
2) Add launch metadata fields to Linear ticket template and update triage checklist (owner: Priya Nair) — due 2026-03-08
3) Wire up gating automation to Slack alerts and dashboards (ENG-4123) — ENG to estimate and mark dependency
4) Run pilot pulse (runtime + console small feature) during 2026-W12 window and capture telemetry
